subject: Data lifecycle carve-out: PII retention & residency follow-up
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.co>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rajan <priya.raj@cardiovue.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's call — PII retention & residency

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good overview. Two quick items we need to lock down before we can advance to legal/procurement:

1) Can Redwood support a hard "zero retention" posture for PII (names, SSNs, patient identifiers) for API requests originating from our EU region?
2) If not, what are the shortest practical retention windows for request/response logs and KV caches, and can those be scoped to a per-customer policy?
3) Do you provide on-demand deletion APIs and proof-of-deletion (for audit)?

Attached are the meeting notes Priya captured.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up call if useful.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Integrations, MedSys Health
liam.oconnor@medsys.co
+44 20 7123 4567

Attachment: meeting-notes-20260818.txt

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rajan <priya.raj@cardiovue.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's call — PII retention & residency

Hi Liam — great talking earlier. Recap and concrete options below so you can take something to legal/procurement. I'm copying Ben (sales engineering) and Marissa (security/compliance) for any technical/legal clarifications.

Short answers up front:
- Hard 0-retention for PII on the hosted Redwood API is not available out-of-the-box.
- We can offer per-customer reduced retention windows, stronger redaction/pseudonymization, and Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for true customer-controlled zero retention.

Options (ordered by confidence/effort):
1) Hosted — Short retention pilot (3-day minimal logs) + on-demand deletion APIs + pseudonymization: lowest friction, fastest to run a pilot.
2) Hosted — 7-day minimal logs with additional aggregation and automatic PII redaction (we can exclude full request bodies from logs for fields you flag).
3) Private (VPC or on-prem) — you control persistence; Redwood can enable a 0-retention mode at the customer-managed storage layer. Requires procurement and deployment lead time (6–10 weeks typical).

What we'll produce for you this week:
- Redwood data retention options doc (summary table + security controls) — attached.
- SOC 2 summary and evidence points we can share with procurement.
- A proposed minimal concession (draft) that Ben will prepare if you want a short-term path to contracting.

Ask from you: please confirm which option you'd like us to draft (1, 2, or 3) and whether EU-only scoping is required. Also confirm whether you need explicit proof-of-deletion artifacts included in the MOPA/contract.

Next steps:
- If you pick option 1 or 2, we'll draft a tailored pilot SOW and a MOPA clause for deletion and retention SLA.
- If you pick option 3, we'll start internal onboarding with our Private deployment team and share timelines.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.co>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rajan <priya.raj@cardiovue.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up from today's call — proposed pilot concession (draft)

Liam — looping back with a concrete draft to unblock procurement. Below is the short concession we'd be willing to pilot while we evaluate Private deployment timelines. This is intended as a time-boxed, technical-side commitment (not a full legal concession) — procurement/legal will need the usual MOPA/contract language.

Proposed pilot concession (summary):
- Scope: EU-region traffic only; applies to request/response logs and KV cache entries.
- Retention: 7 calendar days for request/response logs (raw request bodies excluded when PII fields are flagged). Aggregated telemetry and billing metadata retained for 90 days.
- Pseudonymization: Redwood will apply per-request reversible pseudonymization for fields you designate; keys are rotated every 30 days.
- On-demand deletion: API to delete request/response logs for a given customer_id within 24 hours of request; proof-of-deletion token issued to the requester.
- Evidence: SOC 2 summary + sample deletion token workflow to be included as an addendum.
- Timing: Pilot activation within 2 business days of signed SOW; pilot runs for 30 days.

Attachments: proposed-concession-7d.docx (draft text for the MOPA).

If that sounds acceptable as an interim step, we can prep a short MOPA appendix and route to procurement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

> On Aug 18, 2026, at 11:20 AM, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com> wrote:
>
> > Hi Liam — great talking earlier. Recap and concrete options below...

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rajan <priya.raj@cardiovue.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up from today's call — proposed pilot concession (draft)

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and closer to what procurement needs. A few clarifying items before we route to legal: 

1) The 7-day window is acceptable as an interim pilot, provided the on-demand deletion API is demonstrable and we receive a sample proof-of-deletion token during the pilot.
2) Can you confirm the deletion API scope includes KV cache invalidation (not just request logs)?
3) For pseudonymization: reversible is acceptable for trial, but we will want irreversible hashing for production. Can you include a note about options?

If you can confirm (1) KV cache deletion is included and (2) you'll include the proof-of-deletion example, we'll ask legal to review the MOPA draft.

Also, please circulate the HUBSPOT deal link and the SOW timeline so procurement has a single place to reference.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
MedSys Health

Attachment: signed-mopa-request.pdf

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rajan <priya.raj@cardiovue.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up from today's call — proposed pilot concession (draft)

Liam — quick confirmations to unblock legal: 

1) KV cache: included. The pilot deletion API will invalidate request logs and KV cache entries associated with the customer_id and return a deletion token. We'll include an example token and the verification endpoint in the MOPA appendix.
2) Proof-of-deletion: we'll produce a signed proof-of-deletion token (JSON Web Signature) that includes deletion timestamp, scope, and Red ID. Sample token flow will be in the pilot SOW.
3) Pseudonymization vs irreversible hashing: for the pilot we'll support reversible pseudonymization (to enable debugging). Production options include irreversible hashing or customer-controlled encryption keys via KMS for true non-reversible transforms; we'll add language to the SOW to capture both paths.

Next deliverables (we'll send today):
- MOPA appendix draft (link included) and the draft SOW timeline (pilot start within 2 business days of signed MOPA).
- HubSpot deal link and single-point-of-truth folder (Drive link below).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retention-pilot
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/record/67890

I'll follow up with Marissa on evidence artifacts for procurement. If that aligns, please have legal send me the MOPA redlines and we'll turn around the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
